title: I've wanted to make my own game for ages. AI finally got me started, but finishing it is a different story.
author: Kanzes
selftext:
I've wanted to make my own game for years, but never really knew where to start.

AI tools like Claude finally made it possible for me to give it a shot. It's been a lot of trial and error, but seeing everything slowly come together has been pretty exciting.

Here's one of my favorite parts so far, evolving a fighter from 1★ all the way to 3★.

If anyone's curious, here is my Steam page:  
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5409210/BLACKBELL/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5409210/BLACKBELL/)

Still a long way from release though. I'm looking at March 27 release. There's a lot more I want to experiment with before calling it finished. For anyone else making games with AI, how's your experience been so far? especially for that last 20%?

comments.author: i_rate_slop
comments.body: I like the art style but the animations are a lot. Obviously you do you, but normally in these sorts of games the cards are still and then once you put them in play they "come alive" and are moving.

replies.author: Kanzes
replies.body:
That's actually a really good point! I was trying to make everything feel like an old cartoon, but I can see how having everything moving at once could get distracting lol.

I might experiment with keeping the cards calmer and letting the characters really come alive during battles instead. Thanks for pointing that out, appreciate it

comments.author: Ill-Past4609
comments.body: What animation pipeline did you use ?

replies.author: Kanzes
replies.body: I use Astra & Opus to help with the sprite animations and animation logic, then integrate everything into Godot and tweak the timing and movement in-game. And after that lots and lots trial and error, probably takes me around 1 month back and forth from to get it right!

replies.author: Ill-Past4609
replies.body: Niiice!  So you’re using code? To animate or spritesheets via codex ?

replies.author: rrcecil
replies.body:
I’ve been following that pipeline!

Though I stopped using Astra since it uses the same model and I’ve cut way back on tokens

comments.body: Any info on your art process?
